To find the inverse of the matrix \(\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\), we can use the formula for the inverse of a 2x2 matrix. The inverse of a matrix \(\begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix}\) is given by 

\[
\frac{1}{ad - bc} \begin{bmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{bmatrix}
\]

First, we need to determine the determinant \(ad - bc\):

- Here, \(a = 2\), \(b = 1\), \(c = 1\), and \(d = 3\).
- The determinant is \(2(3) - 1(1) = 6 - 1 = 5\).

Now we can use the determinant to find the inverse:

\[
\begin{bmatrix} 3 & -1 \\ -1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}
\]

Now multiply by the reciprocal of the determinant:

\[
\frac{1}{5} \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -1 \\ -1 & 2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \frac{3}{5} & -\frac{1}{5} \\ -\frac{1}{5} & \frac{2}{5} \end{bmatrix}
\]

Thus, the inverse of the matrix is

\[
\begin{bmatrix} \frac{3}{5} & -\frac{1}{5} \\ -\frac{1}{5} & \frac{2}{5} \end{bmatrix}
\]

Final answer: \(\begin{bmatrix} \frac{3}{5} & -\frac{1}{5} \\ -\frac{1}{5} & \frac{2}{5} \end{bmatrix}\)
